title: MOSAIC: Addressing Disproportionate Task-Modality Dependencies via Modality-Partitioned Gradient Routing
abstract: arXiv:2610.41004v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In multi-task settings, combining multiple modalities allows task representations to draw on signals that a single modality alone would not capture. However, individual tasks may depend disproportionately on particular modalities, a structure that conventional fusion-based architectures do not model explicitly, instead enforcing a unified representation space. Consequently, a task's gradients can affect parameters tied to modalities it barely relies on, leaving features that compromise between competing demands. Although prior work has explored task-weighting and loss-balancing strategies, their effectiveness is limited by the absence of explicit modality separation, preventing models from optimising each modality according to its task-specific importance. translated_title: MOSAIC：通过模态划分的梯度路由解决任务与模态间的非对称依赖问题
translated_abstract: 在多任务设置中，融合多种模态可以让任务表征利用单一模态无法捕捉的信号。然而，各个任务可能不成比例地依赖于某些特定模态，而传统的基于融合的架构并未显式地对这种结构进行建模，而是强制采用统一的表示空间。因此，一个任务的梯度可能会影响其几乎不依赖的模态所关联的参数，导致特征在不同需求之间相互妥协。尽管先前的工作已经探索了任务加权和损失平衡等策略，但由于缺乏显式的模态分离，其有效性受到限制，使模型无法根据各模态对特定任务的重要性进行优化。为了解决这些局限，我们提出了MOSAIC（具有模态间交叉注意力的模态分离架构），它在保留单模态表征的同时，实现了受控的……
tldr: 提出MOSAIC架构，通过模态分离与模态划分的梯度路由显式建模多任务学习中各任务对特定模态的非对称依赖，在保留单模态表征的同时避免跨模态的梯度干扰。
en_tdlr: MOSAIC addresses disproportionate task-modality dependencies in multi-task learning via a modality-separated architecture with modality-partitioned gradient routing and inter-modal cross-attention, preserving unimodal representations while preventing cross-modality gradient interference.
